editorial.summary:
Eight US states have filed lawsuits against OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT poses safety risks and harms children, according to UPI, China Daily Hong Kong and NBC News. Outlets in Kansas, Arkansas and Iowa reported that their attorneys general are among those taking part in the legal action.

Business Insider reported that the states' demands range from deleting data to halting AI testing. Open Magazine framed the suits around concerns that users treat ChatGPT as a confidant. Law Commentary separately reported an accusation that children's ChatGPT data was used to train AI, with a family demanding that the company share it.
editorial.whyItMatters: The suits add legal pressure on a leading AI lab over how its chatbot treats young users and handles their data, which could shape safety obligations for consumer AI products.
keyFacts: Eight US states have sued OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT harms children (NBC News, UPI).
Kansas, Arkansas and Iowa are among the states involved, according to KSN.com, FOX16.com and The Gazette.
Business Insider reported the states' demands include data deletion and halting AI testing.
editorial.note: The Law Commentary report concerns a family's demand over children's data used for AI training, which may be a separate matter from the state lawsuits.

reports.title: OpenAI accuses former employee of leaking intel on AI device to Apple

reports.summary: Hours before Apple and the ChatGPT maker were due to face off in court, a new allegation delayed the showdown An ⁠ OpenAI employee who left the ChatGPT maker for Apple sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal ⁠account and later ⁠made a presentation ​about the unreleased product to senior…

editorial.summary:
OpenAI has accused a former employee who left for Apple of leaking information about an unreleased AI device, according to CNN and The Guardian. The allegation surfaced just hours before Apple and the ChatGPT maker were due to face off in court, and The Guardian reported that it delayed the showdown.

According to The Guardian, the employee sent more than 100 files about the unreleased product to a personal account. The report said the employee later made a presentation about the unreleased product to senior staff. CNN described the claim as OpenAI accusing the former employee of leaking intelligence on the AI device to Apple.
editorial.whyItMatters: The dispute shows how intense competition over AI hardware is becoming between OpenAI and Apple, and how closely labs guard unreleased product plans.
keyFacts: OpenAI accuses a former employee who moved to Apple of leaking details of an unreleased AI device, per CNN and The Guardian.
The Guardian reported the employee sent more than 100 files about the product to a personal account.
The Guardian said the employee later gave a presentation on the product to senior staff.
The allegation came hours before an Apple and OpenAI court hearing and delayed it, according to The Guardian.

editorial.summary:
Google DeepMind said it is working with the Singapore government on a fine-tuned AI model aimed at detecting scams. According to the company, the effort involves GovTech Singapore and uses lightweight Gemma models that run on-device. The company said these models are designed to intercept conversational scams within private chats, with no cloud data egress.

The only source describing the event is Google DeepMind itself, so the account reflects the company's own description of the collaboration. No independent outlets were included in the material reviewed.
editorial.whyItMatters: The project shows an approach in which AI safety tools for fraud run locally on devices rather than sending private messages to the cloud. It offers a concrete example of government and frontier lab cooperation on AI-driven harm prevention.
keyFacts: Google DeepMind and the Singapore government are collaborating on a fine-tuned AI model for scam detection, according to Google DeepMind.
The project involves GovTech Singapore, the company said.
The models are lightweight Gemma models that run on-device, the company said.
The models are designed to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress, according to the company.
